english.title: Engage in controlling / coercive behaviour in an intimate / family relationship
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) repeatedly or continuously engaged in behaviour which was controlling or coercive, namely **(..SPECIFY THE BEHAVIOUR AND, WHERE NECESSARY, THE DATES OF SEPARATE INCIDENTS..), towards **(..SPECIFY NAME OF VICTIM..), to whom, at the time of the behaviour, you were personally connected in that **(..SPECIFY THE NATURE OF THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN DEFENDANT AND VICTIM..), that behaviour having a serious effect on

(A)_[him]_
(B)_[her]_

and you knew or ought to have known that the behaviour would have a serious effect on

(C)_[him]_
(D)_[her]_
english.legislation: Contrary to section 76(1) and (11) of the Serious Crime Act 2015.

english.notes:
(i) Section 68 of the Domestic Abuse Act (brought into force by SI 2023/406 5th April 2023), amended the definition of “personally connected”. The definition of 'personally connected' will vary for offences committed before and after the 5th April 2023. The definition of 'personally connected' for offences before the 5th April being -
76(2) A and B are 'personally connected' if -

(a) A is in an intimate personal relationship with B, or
(b) A and B live together and -

(i) they are members of the same family, or
(ii) they have previously been in an intimate personal relationship with each other.

76(6) For the purposes of subsection (2)(b)(i) A and B are members of the same family if -

(a) they are, or have been, married to each other;
(b) they are, or have been, civil partners of each other;
(c) they are relatives;
(d) they have agreed to marry one another (whether or not the agreement has been terminated);
(e) they have entered into a civil partnership agreement (whether or not the agreement has been terminated);
(f) they are both parents of the same child;
(g) they have, or have had, parental responsibility for the same child.

Section 68 of the Domestic Abuse Act 2021, brought into force on the 5th April 2023 by SI 2023/406 omitted subsection (2), amended (6) and inserted (6A) of/into section 76 of the Serious Crime Act 2015.
(ii) Defences and exemptions for this offence can be found in section 76.
(iii) See section 76A of the Serious Crime Act 2015 regarding the committing of this offence outside the UK by a UK national or a person habitually resident in England and Wales.

other.penalty:
Summary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and / or a fine.
Indictment: maximum 5 years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Note
The maximum penalty on summary conviction depends on the general limit in a magistrates’ court and may be 6 or 12 months depending on the date of conviction, see section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2020.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
